rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (471.07, best so far) kept the iteration 1 geometry and set base_speed to 1.1. The oval now finishes 20 of 20 at a mean of 1.96 s, so there is room under the 3.0 s limit. The s-bend still ends off track in 17 of 20 runs, with mean max_error 0.0598 m, right at the 0.06 m limit. The slalom has 0 finishes, progress 0.10 and max_error 0.0617 m, which is above the limit, and it records 0 line-loss events, so line loss is not the cause. The Evaluator's rule for this case is to lower base_speed to 1.0, since speed has moved max_error in every iteration so far (1.6 to 1.3 to 1.1 each reduced bend error). Change: base_speed 1.1 to 1.0. Everything else stays fixed (geometry as iteration 1, kp 1.6, kd 0.5, ki 0, sensor_weights -2..2, line_loss last_direction) so the race isolates the speed effect. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error drop below 0.06 m, so more runs finish those tracks. The oval mean time should rise from about 1.96 s to about 2.2 s, still under 3.0 s. Risk: at speed 1.0 the robot may be too slow to reach progress 0.995 on the slalom or stall. Next measurements: per-track finish rate, max_error and completion_time. If the oval time exceeds about 2.8 s, go back toward 1.05. If the slalom still exceeds 0.06 m at 1.0, the next lever is kd, not speed.
